# Model and source

```{r model-meta, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
mod_fun <- readModelDb("Liu_2023_mAb_mouse_pbpk")
mod_obj <- rxode2::rxode(mod_fun)
cat("* Citation: ", mod_obj$reference, "\n", sep = "")
cat("* Description: ", mod_obj$description, "\n", sep = "")
```

* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1080/19420862.2023.2263926>
* Supplement (Supplementary Methods 1-3, Supplementary Tables S1-S3, Supplementary Figures S1-S2): <https://doi.org/10.1080/19420862.2023.2263926>
* Upstream platform model: Shah DK, Betts AM. J Pharmacokinet Pharmacodyn. 2012;39(1):67-86, <https://doi.org/10.1007/s10928-011-9232-2> (also packaged as `Shah_2012_mAb_PBPK`)

# Population

Liu 2023 produced 83 antibodies on a single invariant scaffold - an aglycosylated
human IgG1z stable-effector-functionless (SEFL) 2.2 isotype of the G1m17 allotype,
carrying an N297G mutation to remove Fc-gamma-receptor binding plus R292C/V302C to
install a thermostabilising disulfide. The 83 Fv domains were chosen to span a broad
range of physicochemical behaviour across 33 different target antigens, without
regard to target biology. Nineteen antibodies with mouse cross-reactivity (potential
target-mediated disposition) and eight with observed immunogenicity were removed,
leaving **56 antibodies** with clean linear mouse PK.

Each antibody was dosed at **2 mg/kg IV bolus** via the lateral tail vein into female
BALB/c mice aged 6-8 weeks, using a cassette strategy of up to five antibodies per
animal (combined antibody load 10 mg/kg; `n = 3` animals per time point, mean profiles
used for modelling). Serum was assayed by multiplex electrochemiluminescent
immunoassay. Across the 56-antibody panel, AUC(0-672 h) spanned roughly eightfold
(1.74e6 to 1.38e7 ng*h/mL) and clearance about tenfold (2.55 to 26.4 mL/day/kg);
only six antibodies exceeded the in-house 12 mL/day/kg fast-clearance threshold.

A separate panel of **14 monospecific antibodies** (Ab85-Ab98), constructed in the same
SEFL2.2 format from bispecifics known to have poor PK, was run as an a-priori
validation set and deliberately enriched for fast clearance.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Liu_2023_mAb_mouse_pbpk")()$population`.

# Model structure

The model is the Shah & Betts 2012 platform PBPK model: 15 tissues (heart, lung,
muscle, skin, adipose, bone, brain, kidney, liver, small intestine, large intestine,
pancreas, thymus, spleen, "other") connected by plasma and lymph flow, each divided
into a vascular, an endosomal and an interstitial space, plus a central plasma pool
and a lymph node. Antibody enters the interstitium by convection through the
`L * (1 - sigma_V)` paracellular route and enters the endothelial endosome by
fluid-phase pinocytosis `CLup`. In the endosome it binds FcRn (`Kon`/`Koff`); bound
complex recycles to the vascular space (fraction `FR = 0.715`) or to the interstitium
(`1 - FR`), and FcRn-unbound antibody is degraded at `Kdeg`. Because none of the
antibodies bind a mouse antigen, no target-mediated term is present. This gives 77 ODE
states in the packaged model (15 tissues x 5 states, plus plasma and lymph node).

Liu 2023 layered the Chen & Balthasar inter-antibody variability formalism onto that
platform: a coefficient `F1` multiplies the pinocytotic uptake `CLup`, and a
coefficient `F2` multiplies organ lymphatic flow. `F1` and `F2` were first estimated
for each of the 56 antibodies individually. Only `F1` clustered against the in-vitro
assay panel - specifically against heparin-chromatography retention time - so the
final model expresses `F1` as a sigmoidal function of `HEPARIN_RT` and fixes `F2` at
the panel median:

$$F_1 = a + \frac{b - a}{1 + \left(\frac{c}{\mathrm{HEPARIN\_RT}}\right)^{d}}$$

with `a` = 0.67, `b` = 3.65, `c` = 17.7 min and `d` = 22.7 estimated by simultaneously
fitting the 53 retained training antibodies (Table 2), and `F2` = 1.45.

# Source trace

Per-parameter provenance is also recorded as an in-file comment beside every `ini()`
entry in `inst/modeldb/pharmacokinetics/Liu_2023_mAb_mouse_pbpk.R`.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `F1` sigmoid form | `a + (b - a) / (1 + (c / HEPARIN_RT)^d)` | Liu 2023 Eq 1 (Results, "Fitting of the PBPK model incorporating the Heparin_RT covariate") and Eq 2 (Materials and methods, "Simultaneous fitting of antibody PK using full PBPK model"); repeated in Supplementary Methods 2, "Equations for Organ Sub-Compartment" |
| `lclup_scale_min` (`a`) | 0.67 (CV% 1.28) | Liu 2023 Table 2 |
| `lclup_scale_max` (`b`) | 3.65 (CV% 3.37) | Liu 2023 Table 2 |
| `lrt50_clup_scale` (`c`) | 17.7 min (CV% 0.543) | Liu 2023 Table 2 |
| `lhill_clup_scale` (`d`) | 22.7 (CV% 7.89) | Liu 2023 Table 2 |
| `llymph_scale` (`F2`) | 1.45, fixed | Liu 2023 Results: "we fixed F2 to 1.45, the median F2 value in this panel" |
| `lclup` (`CLup`) | 0.24 L/h/L, fixed | Liu 2023 Materials and methods, "Individual fitting of antibody PK using the base PBPK model": "the parameter glossary and values are the same as in Shah and Betts except that the CLup value is set to 0.24 L/h/L" |
| `lfcrn` (`FcRn`) | 4.98e-5 mol/L, fixed | Shah & Betts 2012 Table 6 (inherited unchanged; Liu 2023 reference 36) |
| `lkdeg` (`Kdeg`) | 42.9 1/h, fixed | Shah & Betts 2012 Table 6 |
| `lclnlf` (`C_LNLF`) | 9.1, fixed | Shah & Betts 2012 Table 6 |
| `lkon` (`Kon,FcRn`) | 8.06e7 1/M/h (mouse), fixed | Shah & Betts 2012 text p.73, mouse value |
| `lkoff` (`Koff,FcRn`) | 6.55 1/h (mouse), fixed | Shah & Betts 2012 text p.73, mouse value |
| `FR` = 0.715, `sigma_IS` = 0.2 | constants in `model()` | Shah & Betts 2012 text p.73 |
| `sigma_V` per tissue (0.85 / 0.90 / 0.95 / 0.99) | constants in `model()` | Shah & Betts 2012 text p.73 (assigned by capillary pore size) |
| Mouse organ volumes and plasma flows | see `model()` | Shah & Betts 2012 Table 1, "Physiological model parameters used for mouse (28 g male)" |
| Lymph flow `L_ORG = 0.002 * PLQ_ORG` | ratio | Liu 2023 Supplementary Methods 2, "Lymph Flows" (equivalently Shah & Betts 2012: lymph flow 500-fold lower than plasma flow) |
| `L_LIVER = 0.002 * (PLQ_LIVER + PLQ_LIVER,UPSTREAM)` | flow | Liu 2023 Supplementary Methods 2, "Lymph Flows" |
| `L_LYMPH = C_LNLF * PLQ_LUNG` | flow | Liu 2023 Supplementary Methods 2, "Lymph Flows" |
| `CL_UP,ORG = CL_UP * V_E,ORG` (pinocytosis scaled by each organ's own endosomal volume) | n/a | Liu 2023 Supplementary Methods 2, "Equations for Organ Sub-Compartment" |
| Plasma / lymph-node / vascular / endosomal / interstitial ODEs | n/a | Liu 2023 Supplementary Methods 2, "Essential differential equations" |
| `HEPARIN_RT` per antibody | 2.92-32.6 min | Liu 2023 Supplementary Table S1 |
| Observed AUC, half-life, clearance per antibody | see cohort chunk | Liu 2023 Supplementary Table S1 |
| Individually estimated `F1` and `F2` per antibody | see cohort chunk | Liu 2023 Supplementary Table S2 |
| Validation-set %PE and fast-clearance classification | see validation chunk | Liu 2023 Supplementary Table S3 |
| Published model curves | digitized | Liu 2023 Figures 4a, 4b, 5 and 6 (see the `digitized-curves` chunk) |

# Virtual cohort

There is no between-subject random-effect layer in this model: inter-antibody
variability is carried entirely by `HEPARIN_RT`. The "cohort" is therefore the
antibody panel itself - one deterministic mouse per antibody, 70 in total (56
training + 14 validation), well inside the 200-per-arm cap.

`HEPARIN_RT`, the observed AUC(0-672 h), half-life and clearance, and the individually
estimated `F1` and `F2` are transcribed from Liu 2023 Supplementary Tables S1 and S2;
the validation-set %PE from Supplementary Table S3.

```{r cohort}

) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    id = dplyr::row_number(),
    # Liu 2023 excluded Ab76 (atypical profile) and the two nonspecific-binding
    # false positives Ab37 and Ab30 from the 53-antibody covariate fit.
    fitted = panel_set == "training" & !ab %in% c("Ab76", "Ab37", "Ab30")
  )

# Study constants. Body weight is the Shah & Betts 2012 mouse parameter set the
# model is built on (28 g); it reproduces Supplementary Table S1's clearances,
# e.g. Ab1 dose / AUC = 5.6e4 ng / 7.97e6 ng*h/mL = 0.0070 mL/h vs 0.00687 reported.
bw_kg <- 0.028
dose_mg_kg <- 2
mw_g_per_mol <- 150000    # nominal aglycosylated human IgG1; see Assumptions
dose_nmol <- dose_mg_kg * bw_kg * 1e-3 / mw_g_per_mol * 1e9

sample_times <- sort(unique(c(
  0, 0.0833, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12,
  seq(24, 168, by = 12), seq(192, 672, by = 24)
)))

events <- rxode2::et(amt = dose_nmol, cmt = "plasma", id = ab_panel$id) |>
  rxode2::et(sample_times, id = ab_panel$id) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    ab_panel |> dplyr::select(id, ab, panel_set, HEPARIN_RT, cl_obs, fitted),
    by = "id"
  )

stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod_fun,
  events = events,
  keep = c("ab", "panel_set", "HEPARIN_RT", "cl_obs", "fitted"),
  atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-8
) |>
  as.data.frame()

stopifnot(dplyr::n_distinct(sim$id) == nrow(ab_panel), !anyNA(sim$Cc))
```

# Replicate published figures

The published curves overlaid on Figures 4, 5 and 6 below were digitized from the
published figures of Liu 2023: each line's position was read against its own
panel's axis ticks. They are the authors' model curves, not observations. Figure 6
is printed at the smallest scale of the three, so its values are the least precise.

```{r digitized-curves}
# Liu 2023 Figure 5: the 20 curves are F1 = 0.4 * 10^(k / 19), k = 0..19, i.e.
# log-spaced from 0.4 to 4 as the log10(F1) colour bar shows. The k = 8 curve
# (F1 = 1.05) is drawn in white and cannot be read. Curves k = 17-19 reach the
# 10 ng/mL axis floor before 698 h; their crossing times are recorded as
# conc = 10 at that time. Before about 24 h only k = 0 and k = 19 separate.
fig5_k <- 0:19
fig5_f1 <- 0.4 * 10^(fig5_k / 19)
fig5_pub <- rbind(
  data.frame(k = fig5_k, time = 300,
             conc = c(19600, 18000, 16400, 14800, 13200, 11600, 10100, 8710, NA, 6120,
                      5040, 4040, 3200, 2480, 1890, 1400, 1020, 718, 506, 340)),
  data.frame(k = fig5_k, time = 494.9,
             conc = c(12800, 11100, 9610, 8180, 6870, 5600, 4500, 3550, NA, 2040,
                      1490, 1060, 728, 488, 316, 197, 120, 70.5, 40.1, 21.6)),
  data.frame(k = fig5_k, time = 697.6,
             conc = c(8180, 6770, 5540, 4440, 3440, 2620, 1950, 1400, NA, 651,
                      423, 264, 158, 91.0, 50.0, 26.2, 13.2, NA, NA, NA)),
  data.frame(k = rep(c(0, 19), each = 6), time = rep(c(24, 48, 72, 100, 150, 200), 2),
             conc = c(38600, 34500, 32100, 29300, 26800, 24400,
                      19100, 12600, 8610, 5730, 2800, 1390)),
  data.frame(k = 17:19, time = c(652, 597, 544), conc = 10)
) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(conc)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(F1 = fig5_f1[k + 1])

# At 2.2 h all 20 published Figure 5 curves still overlap, inside this band.
fig5_band_2h <- c(time = 2.2, lower = 37100, upper = 53400)

# Liu 2023 Figures 4a, 4b (fitted lines of the final covariate model) and 6
# (a-priori predicted lines), read at fixed times; NA where a data marker
# covers the line or the line has ended.
fig46_times <- c(100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600, 690)
fig46_pub <- rbind(
  data.frame(ab = "Ab1",  figure = "4a", time = fig46_times,
             conc = c(23200, 16700, 12100, 8730, 6480, 4560, 3380)),
  data.frame(ab = "Ab20", figure = "4a", time = fig46_times,
             conc = c(23200, 16700, 12100, 8500, 6140, 4440, 3290)),
  data.frame(ab = "Ab50", figure = "4a", time = fig46_times,
             conc = c(22100, 14700, 9730, 6450, NA, 2830, 1980)),
  data.frame(ab = "Ab75", figure = "4a", time = fig46_times,
             conc = c(20600, 13600, 9060, 6040, NA, 2650, 1840)),
  data.frame(ab = "Ab63", figure = "4b", time = fig46_times,
             conc = c(23100, 16500, 11800, 8560, 6120, 4430, 3280)),
  data.frame(ab = "Ab84", figure = "4b", time = fig46_times,
             conc = c(12100, 5270, 2350, 1070, 530, 213, 104)),
  data.frame(ab = "Ab39", figure = "4b", time = fig46_times,
             conc = c(10400, 4110, 1630, 647, 263, 104, 46.5)),
  data.frame(ab = "Ab14", figure = "4b", time = fig46_times,
             conc = c(5850, 1530, 411, 110, 29.9, NA, NA)),
  data.frame(ab = "Ab36", figure = "4b", time = fig46_times,
             conc = c(5890, 1540, 413, 111, 30.3, NA, NA)),
  data.frame(ab = "Ab97", figure = "6", time = fig46_times,
             conc = c(23500, 16800, 12000, 8570, 6390, 4380, NA)),
  data.frame(ab = "Ab98", figure = "6", time = fig46_times,
             conc = c(6260, 1700, 473, 134, 36.5, 10.4, NA))
) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(conc))

# The packaged model for the digitized antibodies, on a fine time grid.
fine_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 900, by = 2), 1, 2.2, 494.9, 697.6)))
digit_abs <- ab_panel |>
  dplyr::filter(ab %in% fig46_pub$ab) |>
  dplyr::transmute(id = dplyr::row_number(), ab, HEPARIN_RT)
ev_digit <- rxode2::et(amt = dose_nmol, cmt = "plasma", id = digit_abs$id) |>
  rxode2::et(fine_times, id = digit_abs$id) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::left_join(digit_abs, by = "id")
sim_digit <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_fun, events = ev_digit, keep = "ab",
                             atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-8) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::mutate(conc = Cc * mw_g_per_mol / 1e3)
stopifnot(setequal(unique(sim_digit$ab), unique(fig46_pub$ab)))

# Ab1 and Ab20 sit on the same F1 plateau, so their published lines are the same
# curve read twice; the spread between the two readings measures the precision.
repeat_pair <- merge(fig46_pub[fig46_pub$ab == "Ab1", c("time", "conc")],
                     fig46_pub[fig46_pub$ab == "Ab20", c("time", "conc")], by = "time")
digit_spread_pct <- 100 * max(abs(repeat_pair$conc.x / repeat_pair$conc.y - 1))
stopifnot(nrow(repeat_pair) == 7, digit_spread_pct < 10)
n_fig4_digit <- dplyr::n_distinct(fig46_pub$ab[fig46_pub$figure != "6"])
```

The values are written to three significant figures, but that overstates their
precision: Ab1 and Ab20 share the same `F1`, so their published lines are one curve
read twice, and the two readings differ by up to `r round(digit_spread_pct, 1)`%.

## Figure 3d - sigmoidal relationship between `F1` and heparin retention time

```{r figure-3d}
# Replicates Figure 3d of Liu 2023: individually estimated F1 (points) against
# Heparin_RT, with the fitted sigmoid (red) and the 16.5 min flag threshold
# (blue dashed). Ab37 and Ab30 (open circles in the paper) were excluded from
# the fit; Ab76 (Heparin_RT 31.5 min) is off-scale in the paper's panel.
f1_curve <- tibble::tibble(HEPARIN_RT = seq(2, 24, length.out = 400)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(F1 = 0.67 + (3.65 - 0.67) / (1 + (17.7 / HEPARIN_RT)^22.7))

ab_panel |>
  dplyr::filter(panel_set == "training", !is.na(f1_indiv), ab != "Ab76") |>
  ggplot(aes(HEPARIN_RT, f1_indiv)) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = fitted), size = 2) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = 16, `FALSE` = 1),
                     labels = c(`TRUE` = "in 53-mAb fit", `FALSE` = "excluded (Ab37, Ab30)"),
                     name = NULL) +
  geom_line(data = f1_curve, aes(HEPARIN_RT, F1), colour = "red", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 16.5, colour = "blue", linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(x = "Heparin retention time (min)", y = expression(F[1]),
       title = "Figure 3d - F1 versus heparin chromatography retention time",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 3d of Liu 2023.") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Figure 5 - sensitivity of the plasma profile to `F1`

The paper's Figure 5 sweeps `F1` over 20 log-spaced values from 0.4 to 4
(`F1 = 0.4 * 10^(k / 19)`, k = 0..19). Because the packaged model derives `F1` from
`HEPARIN_RT`, the sweep is done by collapsing the sigmoid's two plateaus onto the
target value (`clup_scale_min = clup_scale_max = F1`), which makes `F1` constant and
independent of the covariate. `F2` stays at the final model's 1.45; the paper does
not state the value used for this figure.

```{r figure-5}
# Replicates Figure 5 of Liu 2023: plasma PK after 2 mg/kg IV for the 20 F1
# values of the published sweep, one id per F1 value.
ev5 <- rxode2::et(amt = dose_nmol, cmt = "plasma", id = seq_along(fig5_f1)) |>
  rxode2::et(fine_times, id = seq_along(fig5_f1))
sweep_params <- data.frame(id = seq_along(fig5_f1),
                           lclup_scale_min = log(fig5_f1), lclup_scale_max = log(fig5_f1),
                           HEPARIN_RT = 10)
sens <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_fun, events = ev5, params = sweep_params,
                        atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-8) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::mutate(k = id - 1, F1 = fig5_f1[id], conc = Cc * mw_g_per_mol / 1e3)

sens |>
  dplyr::filter(time > 0, time <= 700) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, conc, group = k, colour = log10(F1))) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_point(data = fig5_pub, aes(time, conc, fill = log10(F1)), shape = 21,
             colour = "black", size = 1.8, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_errorbar(data = data.frame(time = fig5_band_2h[["time"]],
                                  lower = fig5_band_2h[["lower"]],
                                  upper = fig5_band_2h[["upper"]]),
                aes(x = time, ymin = lower, ymax = upper), width = 12,
                colour = "black", inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(10, 1e5)) +
  scale_colour_gradient2(low = "firebrick", mid = "grey80", high = "navy", midpoint = 0,
                         name = expression(log[10](F[1])), aesthetics = c("colour", "fill")) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Plasma concentration (ng/mL)",
       title = "Figure 5 - sensitivity of plasma PK to F1",
       caption = paste0("Lines: packaged model. Points: Liu 2023 Figure 5, digitized.\n",
                        "The bar at 2.2 h spans all 20 published curves, which still overlap there."))
```

# PKNCA validation

Liu 2023 computed its own non-compartmental parameters with PKNCA (Materials and
methods, "Non-compartmental analysis"), so the same tool is used here on the
simulated profiles.

Clearance and half-life are the comparison metrics of choice because both are
**independent of the assumed antibody molar mass**: the model runs in nmol / nM, and
`CL = dose_nmol / AUC_nM*h` cancels the molar mass that converts the paper's
ng*h/mL AUCs.

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, ab, panel_set)

sim_nca <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  sim_nca,
  sim_nca |> dplyr::distinct(id, ab, panel_set) |> dplyr::mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, ab, panel_set, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | ab + id)

dose_df <- events |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, ab)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | ab + id)

intervals <- data.frame(
  start      = 0,
  end        = Inf,
  cmax       = TRUE,
  tmax       = TRUE,
  auclast    = TRUE,
  aucinf.obs = TRUE,
  half.life  = TRUE,
  cl.obs     = TRUE
)

nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

nca_wide <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  dplyr::select(ab, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  dplyr::left_join(ab_panel, by = "ab") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    # cl.obs is nmol / (nmol/L * h) = L/h; convert to mL/h to match Table S1.
    cl_pred    = cl.obs * 1000,
    thalf_pred = half.life,
    # AUC(0-672 h) in ng*h/mL, for the %PE comparison against Table S3.
    auc_pred   = auclast * mw_g_per_mol / 1e3,
    pe_pred    = 100 * (auc_pred - auc_obs) / auc_obs,
    cl_obs_day_kg  = cl_obs  * 24 / bw_kg,
    cl_pred_day_kg = cl_pred * 24 / bw_kg
  )
```

## Observed versus predicted clearance across the whole panel

```{r obs-pred-cl}
nca_wide |>
  ggplot(aes(cl_obs * 24 / bw_kg, cl_pred * 24 / bw_kg, colour = panel_set)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0) +
  geom_abline(slope = 2, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_abline(slope = 0.5, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 12, colour = "red", linetype = "dotted") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 12, colour = "red", linetype = "dotted") +
  scale_x_log10() + scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Observed CL (mL/day/kg, Supplementary Table S1)",
       y = "Model-predicted CL (mL/day/kg)",
       colour = NULL,
       title = "Observed versus predicted clearance, 70 antibodies",
       caption = "Solid line is unity; dashed lines are 2-fold; dotted red lines are the 12 mL/day/kg fast-clearance threshold.")
```

```{r fold-error-summary}
fold_summary <- nca_wide |>
  dplyr::mutate(fold = cl_pred / cl_obs) |>
  dplyr::group_by(panel_set) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    n = dplyr::n(),
    median_fold = median(fold),
    within_2fold_pct = 100 * mean(fold > 0.5 & fold < 2),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
# Pins the training-panel figures quoted under "Half-life within the
# low-retention plateau" below.
training_fold <- fold_summary[fold_summary$panel_set == "training", ]
stopifnot(training_fold$median_fold > 0.85, training_fold$median_fold < 1,
          training_fold$within_2fold_pct >= 85)

fold_summary |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Panel" = panel_set, "N" = n,
    "Median predicted/observed CL" = median_fold,
    "Within 2-fold (%)" = within_2fold_pct
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Predicted-to-observed clearance ratio by panel.")
```

## Fast-clearance classification of the validation panel

Liu 2023 reports a positive predictive value of 85%, a negative predictive value of
100%, a false-positive rate of 67% and a false-negative rate of 0% when the 14
validation antibodies are classified against the 12 mL/day/kg threshold
(Supplementary Table S3).

The table below carries three classification columns. `Observed (Table S3)` is the
paper's own observed call, transcribed verbatim. `Observed (recomputed)` re-derives it
from Supplementary Table S1's clearance at 28 g. `Predicted` is this model's call.

```{r classification}
# Liu 2023 Supplementary Table S3, "High CL?" columns, transcribed verbatim.
s3_observed  <- c(Ab85 = "Yes", Ab86 = "Yes", Ab87 = "Yes", Ab88 = "Yes", Ab89 = "No",
                  Ab90 = "No",  Ab91 = "Yes", Ab92 = "Yes", Ab93 = "Yes", Ab94 = "Yes",
                  Ab95 = "Yes", Ab96 = "Yes", Ab97 = "No",  Ab98 = "Yes")
s3_predicted <- c(Ab85 = "Yes", Ab86 = "Yes", Ab87 = "Yes", Ab88 = "Yes", Ab89 = "Yes",
                  Ab90 = "Yes", Ab91 = "Yes", Ab92 = "Yes", Ab93 = "Yes", Ab94 = "Yes",
                  Ab95 = "Yes", Ab96 = "Yes", Ab97 = "No",  Ab98 = "Yes")

classif <- nca_wide |>
  dplyr::filter(panel_set == "validation") |>
  dplyr::arrange(as.integer(sub("^Ab", "", ab))) |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    ab,
    `Heparin RT (min)`      = HEPARIN_RT,
    `Observed CL (mL/day/kg)` = round(cl_obs_day_kg, 1),
    `Observed (Table S3)`   = unname(s3_observed[ab]),
    `Observed (recomputed)` = ifelse(cl_obs_day_kg  > 12, "Yes", "No"),
    `Predicted (Table S3)`  = unname(s3_predicted[ab]),
    `Predicted (model)`     = ifelse(cl_pred_day_kg > 12, "Yes", "No"),
    `Published %PE`         = pe_published,
    `Simulated %PE`         = round(pe_pred, 1)
  )

knitr::kable(classif, digits = 1,
             caption = "Validation panel: fast-clearance classification and %PE on AUC(0-672 h). Table S3 columns are Liu 2023 Supplementary Table S3 verbatim.")

stopifnot(identical(classif$`Predicted (model)`, classif$`Predicted (Table S3)`))

metrics <- function(obs, pred) {
  tp <- sum(obs == "Yes" & pred == "Yes"); fp <- sum(obs == "No"  & pred == "Yes")
  tn <- sum(obs == "No"  & pred == "No");  fn <- sum(obs == "Yes" & pred == "No")
  c(tp / (tp + fp), tn / (tn + fn), fp / (fp + tn), fn / (fn + tp))
}

tibble::tibble(
  Metric = c("Positive predictive value", "Negative predictive value",
             "False-positive rate", "False-negative rate"),
  `Model vs Table S3 observed` =
    round(metrics(classif$`Observed (Table S3)`, classif$`Predicted (model)`), 2),
  `Model vs recomputed observed` =
    round(metrics(classif$`Observed (recomputed)`, classif$`Predicted (model)`), 2),
  Published = c(0.85, 1.00, 0.67, 0.00)
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Classification metrics versus Liu 2023 Supplementary Table S3.")
```

The model reproduces Supplementary Table S3's **predicted** classification for all 14
validation antibodies exactly (asserted above), and against the paper's own observed
calls it recovers the published PPV of 85%, NPV of 100%, FPR of 67% and FNR of 0%.

The recomputed-observed column differs for one antibody. Ab87's clearance in
Supplementary Table S1 is 0.0121 mL/h, which is 10.4 mL/day/kg at 28 g - below the
12 mL/day/kg threshold - yet Supplementary Table S3 lists it as observed-high. The
same conversion reproduces the published call for the other 13 antibodies (and the
0.0121 mL/h clearance is itself consistent with Table S1's AUC and the 2 mg/kg dose at
a body weight of about 27 g, so no plausible body weight puts Ab87 above the
threshold). This looks like a borderline inconsistency between the two supplementary
tables rather than anything about the model; classifying Ab87 as observed-low moves
the PPV to 77% and the FPR to 75%. Both readings are shown so a reviewer can see the
provenance of each.

## Comparison against published NCA

The side-by-side comparison below uses eight antibodies spanning the full heparin
retention-time range: three from the low-`F1` plateau, two straddling the 16.5 min
threshold, and three from the high-`F1` plateau.

```{r nca_compare}
compare_abs <- c("Ab20", "Ab1", "Ab51", "Ab97", "Ab39", "Ab14", "Ab85", "Ab98")

published <- ab_panel |>
  dplyr::filter(ab %in% compare_abs) |>
  dplyr::arrange(match(ab, compare_abs)) |>
  dplyr::transmute(ab, auclast = auc_obs, half.life = thalf_obs,
                   cl.obs = cl_obs / 1000)

simulated <- nca_wide |>
  dplyr::filter(ab %in% compare_abs) |>
  dplyr::transmute(ab, auclast = auc_pred, half.life = thalf_pred,
                   cl.obs = cl_pred / 1000)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated     = simulated,
  reference     = published,
  by            = "ab",
  units         = c(auclast = "ng*h/mL", half.life = "h", cl.obs = "L/h"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)

knitr::kable(
  cmp,
  caption = "Simulated versus published NCA (Liu 2023 Supplementary Table S1). * differs from the reference by more than 20%."
)

# Signed percentage differences quoted in the paragraph below, matched by antibody.
pct_diff <- function(param) {
  ref <- published[[param]][match(simulated$ab, published$ab)]
  stats::setNames(100 * (simulated[[param]] / ref - 1), simulated$ab)
}
cl_pct <- pct_diff("cl.obs")
thalf_pct <- pct_diff("half.life")
fmt_pct <- function(x) sprintf("%+.0f%%", x)
plateau_abs <- c("Ab20", "Ab1", "Ab51")
cl_plateau_uL_h <- simulated$cl.obs[simulated$ab %in% plateau_abs] * 1e6
stopifnot(
  setequal(simulated$ab, published$ab),
  diff(range(cl_plateau_uL_h)) / mean(cl_plateau_uL_h) < 0.01,
  abs(cl_pct[["Ab14"]]) < 20, cl_pct[["Ab39"]] > 20, cl_pct[["Ab39"]] < 30,
  cl_pct[["Ab97"]] < -20, cl_pct[["Ab98"]] < -20, cl_pct[["Ab85"]] > 20,
  all(thalf_pct[c("Ab1", "Ab51", "Ab39", "Ab14", "Ab98")] > 20),
  all(thalf_pct[c("Ab20", "Ab85")] < -20), abs(thalf_pct[["Ab97"]]) < 5
)
```

`ncaComparisonTable()` labels PKNCA's `cl.obs` as "CL/F"; dosing here is
intravenous, so that row is plain systemic clearance (no bioavailability term).

The three low-retention antibodies (Ab20, Ab1 and Ab51) sit on the sigmoid's lower
plateau, so the model gives them practically the same profile and clearance,
`r sprintf("%.2f", mean(cl_plateau_uL_h))` uL/h (within 1% of each other), while their reported clearances span
`r sprintf("%.2f", min(published$cl.obs[published$ab %in% plateau_abs]) * 1e6)`-`r sprintf("%.2f", max(published$cl.obs[published$ab %in% plateau_abs]) * 1e6)` uL/h.
The simulated clearance therefore differs by `r fmt_pct(cl_pct[["Ab20"]])` for Ab20,
`r fmt_pct(cl_pct[["Ab1"]])` for Ab1 and `r fmt_pct(cl_pct[["Ab51"]])` for Ab51: one
`F1` per plateau cannot carry that spread (see *Half-life within the low-retention
plateau* below). Of the other five, clearance is within 20% only for Ab14
(`r fmt_pct(cl_pct[["Ab14"]])`) and just outside it for Ab39
(`r fmt_pct(cl_pct[["Ab39"]])`). It is under-predicted for Ab97
(`r fmt_pct(cl_pct[["Ab97"]])`) and Ab98 (`r fmt_pct(cl_pct[["Ab98"]])`) and
over-predicted for Ab85 (`r fmt_pct(cl_pct[["Ab85"]])`). Above the 16.5 min threshold
the sigmoid plateaus at `b` = 3.65, so the model gives all high-retention antibodies
nearly the same clearance and cannot follow the spread among them; the paper notes
"huge mAb PK variability when Heparin_RT is large, leading to PK underprediction
almost 30% of the time". Half-life differs in both directions: it is longer than
reported for Ab1, Ab51, Ab39, Ab14 and Ab98
(`r fmt_pct(min(thalf_pct[c("Ab1", "Ab51", "Ab39", "Ab14", "Ab98")]))` to
`r fmt_pct(max(thalf_pct[c("Ab1", "Ab51", "Ab39", "Ab14", "Ab98")]))`), shorter for
Ab20 (`r fmt_pct(thalf_pct[["Ab20"]])`) and Ab85 (`r fmt_pct(thalf_pct[["Ab85"]])`),
and about equal for Ab97 (`r sprintf("%+.1f%%", thalf_pct[["Ab97"]])`). Where it is longer, part
of the difference is the model itself: its terminal phase is longer than that of the
published model curves (next section, and *Shape of the published model curves*
under Assumptions and deviations). The simulated half-lives are also estimated over
a 672 h window from smooth noise-free profiles, whereas the published ones come from
sparse composite mean profiles (`n = 3` per time point). No parameter was tuned to
improve either comparison.

## Comparison with the published model curves

The digitized curves overlaid on Figures 4, 5 and 6 are the authors' own model
output, so they allow a model-to-model comparison that observations cannot. The
first table pairs every digitized point with the packaged model at the same time;
the checks after it compare the clearance and exposure the published model implies
(Supplementary Tables S1-S3).

```{r published-curves-compare}
# Pair every digitized point with the packaged model at the same time.
f5_pts <- fig5_pub |>
  dplyr::filter(conc > 10) |>
  dplyr::mutate(t_key = round(time, 1)) |>
  dplyr::left_join(sens |> dplyr::transmute(k, t_key = round(time, 1), sim = conc),
                   by = c("k", "t_key"))
f46_pts <- fig46_pub |>
  dplyr::mutate(t_key = round(time, 1)) |>
  dplyr::left_join(sim_digit |> dplyr::transmute(ab, t_key = round(time, 1), sim = conc),
                   by = c("ab", "t_key"))
stopifnot(!anyNA(f5_pts$sim), !anyNA(f46_pts$sim))

pts <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  f5_pts |> dplyr::transmute(figure = "5", curve = sprintf("F1 = %.2f", F1), time,
                             published = conc, simulated = sim),
  f46_pts |> dplyr::transmute(figure, curve = ab, time, published = conc, simulated = sim)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(ratio = simulated / published)

per_curve <- pts |>
  dplyr::group_by(figure, curve) |>
  dplyr::arrange(time, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    n = dplyr::n(),
    first_h = dplyr::first(time), pub_first = dplyr::first(published),
    sim_first = dplyr::first(simulated), ratio_first = dplyr::first(ratio),
    last_h = dplyr::last(time), pub_last = dplyr::last(published),
    sim_last = dplyr::last(simulated), ratio_last = dplyr::last(ratio),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
# On every digitized curve the simulated/published ratio is higher at the last
# digitized time than at the first, and above 1 at the last digitized time.
stopifnot(all(per_curve$n >= 2), all(per_curve$ratio_last > per_curve$ratio_first),
          all(per_curve$ratio_last > 1))

per_curve |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    dplyr::across(c(pub_first, sim_first, pub_last, sim_last),
                  ~ formatC(signif(.x, 3), format = "fg", digits = 3)),
    dplyr::across(c(first_h, last_h), as.character)
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Figure = figure, Curve = curve, Points = n,
    `First time (h)` = first_h, `Published, first` = pub_first,
    `Simulated, first` = sim_first, `Ratio, first` = ratio_first,
    `Last time (h)` = last_h, `Published, last` = pub_last,
    `Simulated, last` = sim_last, `Ratio, last` = ratio_last
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = paste(
    "Packaged model versus the digitized published model curves (ng/mL), at the",
    "first and last digitized time of each curve. Ratio is simulated / published."))

pts |>
  dplyr::mutate(phase = ifelse(time <= 200, "24-200 h", "300-698 h")) |>
  dplyr::group_by(Figure = figure, Phase = phase) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Points = dplyr::n(),
    `Geometric-mean ratio` = exp(mean(log(ratio))),
    `Min ratio` = min(ratio), `Max ratio` = max(ratio),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Simulated / published ratio by figure and phase.")

# Time at which a curve falls to `level`, interpolated on the log scale.
time_at_level <- function(time, conc, level) {
  i <- which(conc < level & time > 0)[1]
  stats::approx(log(conc[c(i - 1, i)]), time[c(i - 1, i)], log(level))$y
}
cross <- fig5_pub |>
  dplyr::filter(conc == 10) |>
  dplyr::rowwise() |>
  dplyr::mutate(sim_time = time_at_level(sens$time[sens$k == k], sens$conc[sens$k == k], 10)) |>
  dplyr::ungroup()
stopifnot(all(cross$sim_time > cross$time))
knitr::kable(
  cross |> dplyr::transmute(`F1` = round(F1, 2), `Published (h)` = time,
                            `Simulated (h)` = round(sim_time)),
  caption = "Time at which the Figure 5 curve falls to 10 ng/mL.")

# Initial phase. Dose / plasma volume (0.944 mL, Shah & Betts 2012 Table 1) is
# the concentration before any distribution.
c0 <- dose_nmol / (0.944 / 1000) * mw_g_per_mol / 1e3
sim_2h <- sens$conc[sens$time == 2.2]
v_1h_mL <- dose_nmol / sens$Cc[sens$time == 1] * 1000
band_pct <- 100 * fig5_band_2h[c("lower", "upper")] / c0
sim_2h_pct <- 100 * range(sim_2h) / c0
stopifnot(length(sim_2h) == 20, max(sim_2h) < fig5_band_2h[["lower"]],
          band_pct[["lower"]] > 60, sim_2h_pct[2] < 55,
          all(v_1h_mL > 1.7), all(v_1h_mL < 2.1))

# Terminal phase: half-life between 300 and 697.6 h for every Figure 5 curve
# readable at both times.
half_life <- function(c1, c2, dt) log(2) * dt / log(c1 / c2)
term <- f5_pts |>
  dplyr::filter(time %in% c(300, 697.6)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(k, F1) |>
  dplyr::filter(dplyr::n() == 2) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    pub_thalf = half_life(conc[time == 300], conc[time == 697.6], 397.6),
    sim_thalf = half_life(sim[time == 300], sim[time == 697.6], 397.6),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(thalf_ratio = sim_thalf / pub_thalf)
stopifnot(nrow(term) == 16, all(term$thalf_ratio > 1.15))

# F2 is not stated for Figure 5; the same sweep with F2 = 1 instead of 1.45.
sens_f2 <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_fun, events = ev5,
                           params = transform(sweep_params, llymph_scale = 0),
                           atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-8) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::transmute(k = id - 1, t_key = round(time, 1), sim_f2 = Cc * mw_g_per_mol / 1e3)
f2_change_pct <- f5_pts |>
  dplyr::left_join(sens_f2, by = c("k", "t_key")) |>
  dplyr::summarise(max_pct = 100 * max(abs(sim_f2 / sim - 1))) |>
  dplyr::pull(max_pct)
stopifnot(f2_change_pct < 15)
```

```{r published-clearance-compare}
# Clearance side 1: the individually estimated F1 and F2 of Supplementary
# Table S2 against the clearance of Supplementary Table S1, for all 56 training
# antibodies. The summary is also given without Ab76 and Ab45, whose individual
# fits Liu 2023 reports did not describe their profiles (Ab76 has a distinct
# steep alpha phase, Ab45 a three-phase profile); a single F1/F2 pair is then not
# expected to reproduce their clearance.
indiv <- ab_panel |>
  dplyr::filter(panel_set == "training") |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = dplyr::row_number())
long_times <- c(seq(0, 2, by = 0.05), seq(2.5, 24, by = 0.5), seq(26, 4000, by = 2))
ev_ind <- rxode2::et(amt = dose_nmol, cmt = "plasma", id = indiv$id) |>
  rxode2::et(long_times, id = indiv$id)
ind_params <- data.frame(id = indiv$id,
                         lclup_scale_min = log(indiv$f1_indiv),
                         lclup_scale_max = log(indiv$f1_indiv),
                         llymph_scale = log(indiv$f2_indiv),
                         HEPARIN_RT = 10)
sim_ind <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_fun, events = ev_ind, params = ind_params,
                           atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-8) |>
  as.data.frame()

# AUC(0-inf) by the linear trapezoid plus a log-linear tail from the last two points.
auc_inf <- function(time, conc) {
  n <- length(time)
  lambda <- log(conc[n - 1] / conc[n]) / (time[n] - time[n - 1])
  sum(diff(time) * (head(conc, -1) + tail(conc, -1)) / 2) + conc[n] / lambda
}
cl_ind <- sim_ind |>
  dplyr::group_by(id) |>
  dplyr::summarise(auc_nM_h = auc_inf(time, Cc), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::left_join(indiv |> dplyr::select(id, ab, cl_obs), by = "id") |>
  dplyr::mutate(cl_sim_mL_h = dose_nmol / auc_nM_h * 1000, ratio = cl_sim_mL_h / cl_obs)
gm_cl_all <- exp(mean(log(cl_ind$ratio)))
within20_cl_all <- sum(abs(cl_ind$ratio - 1) < 0.2)
cl_ind54 <- cl_ind[!cl_ind$ab %in% c("Ab45", "Ab76"), ]
gm_cl_ind <- exp(mean(log(cl_ind54$ratio)))
within20_cl_ind <- sum(abs(cl_ind54$ratio - 1) < 0.2)
stopifnot(nrow(cl_ind) == 56, nrow(cl_ind54) == 54,
          gm_cl_all > 0.9, gm_cl_all < 1.1, within20_cl_all >= 40,
          gm_cl_ind > 0.9, gm_cl_ind < 1.1, within20_cl_ind >= 40)

# Clearance side 2: Supplementary Table S3's %PE together with the observed AUC
# of Table S1 gives the AUC(0-672 h) the published model predicted for each
# validation antibody.
val_auc <- nca_wide |>
  dplyr::filter(panel_set == "validation") |>
  dplyr::mutate(auc_pred_liu = auc_obs * (1 + pe_published / 100),
                ratio = auc_pred / auc_pred_liu)
gm_auc_val <- exp(mean(log(val_auc$ratio)))
stopifnot(nrow(val_auc) == 14, gm_auc_val > 0.9, gm_auc_val < 1.05)

# The AUC in ng*h/mL does not depend on the assumed molar mass: the dose in nmol
# scales with 1 / molar mass and the ng/mL conversion with molar mass, and the
# model is linear at this dose. Re-solving with a molar mass 10% higher pins it.
auc_trapezoid <- function(time, conc) sum(diff(time) * (head(conc, -1) + tail(conc, -1)) / 2)
auc_ng <- function(mw) {
  dose_mw <- dose_mg_kg * bw_kg * 1e-3 / mw * 1e9
  ev_mw <- rxode2::et(amt = dose_mw, cmt = "plasma", id = seq_along(val_auc$HEPARIN_RT)) |>
    rxode2::et(seq(0, 672, by = 1), id = seq_along(val_auc$HEPARIN_RT))
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod_fun, events = ev_mw,
                  params = data.frame(id = seq_along(val_auc$HEPARIN_RT),
                                      HEPARIN_RT = val_auc$HEPARIN_RT),
                  atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-8) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    dplyr::group_by(id) |>
    dplyr::summarise(auc = auc_trapezoid(time, Cc) * mw / 1e3, .groups = "drop") |>
    dplyr::pull(auc)
}
mw_change_pct <- 100 * max(abs(auc_ng(1.1 * mw_g_per_mol) / auc_ng(mw_g_per_mol) - 1))
stopifnot(mw_change_pct < 1)

tibble::tibble(
  Check = c("Table S2 F1/F2 -> CL, against Table S1 CL (all 56 training antibodies)",
            "Same, without Ab45 and Ab76 (54 antibodies)",
            "AUC(0-672 h), against the published model's prediction (Table S3, 14 antibodies)"),
  `Geometric-mean ratio` = c(gm_cl_all, gm_cl_ind, gm_auc_val),
  `Within 20%` = c(sprintf("%d of 56", within20_cl_all), sprintf("%d of 54", within20_cl_ind),
                   sprintf("%d of 14", sum(abs(val_auc$ratio - 1) < 0.2))),
  `Min` = c(min(cl_ind$ratio), min(cl_ind54$ratio), min(val_auc$ratio)),
  `Max` = c(max(cl_ind$ratio), max(cl_ind54$ratio), max(val_auc$ratio))
) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Packaged model / published model, clearance and exposure.")
```

The packaged model matches the published model's clearance and exposure but not the
shape of its curves. With the individually estimated `F1` and `F2` of Supplementary
Table S2 it reproduces the Supplementary Table S1 clearances (geometric-mean ratio
`r sprintf("%.2f", gm_cl_all)` over all 56 training antibodies, `r within20_cl_all` of
them within 20%; `r sprintf("%.2f", gm_cl_ind)` and `r within20_cl_ind` of 54 without
Ab45 and Ab76, whose individual fits did not describe their profiles). Its
validation-set AUCs match those the published model predicted (geometric-mean ratio
`r sprintf("%.2f", gm_auc_val)`); this comparison does not depend on the assumed
molar mass (a 10% higher molar mass changes the simulated AUCs by at most
`r sprintf("%.2f", mw_change_pct)`%), so the remaining offset of about
`r round(100 * abs(1 - gm_auc_val))`% is not a molar-mass effect, and its source is not
determined. The curves differ in shape: at 2.2 h every
simulated Figure 5 curve lies below the whole band of published curves, at the last
digitized time every simulated curve lies above its published counterpart, and on
every digitized curve the simulated/published ratio rises with time. The deviation is
recorded under *Shape of the published model curves* below.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **`F2` placement.** Liu 2023's Results and Figure 2 state that `F2` multiplies
  organ lymphatic flow `L * (1 - sigma)` and that it was fixed to 1.45 in the final
  model, but the differential equations printed in Supplementary Methods 2 contain no
  `F2` term at all (equivalent to `F2` = 1). The model file follows the text: `F2`
  multiplies `L_ORG` in every convective term (vascular-to-interstitial entry,
  interstitial-to-lymph exit, and the matching lymph-node inflow), leaving the bulk
  vascular outflow `PLQ - L` unscaled so that antibody mass is conserved. Setting
  `llymph_scale = log(1)` recovers the supplement's printed equations exactly. Figure 2's
  caption instead describes `F2` as modulating `sigma_V`; that reading is not
  tenable, because the reported individual `F2` estimates run up to 17.6 and would
  drive `sigma_V` above 1 (negative convection).
- **Lung plasma flow is derived, not taken from Table 1.** Shah & Betts 2012 Table 1
  reports 373 mL/h for mouse lung, but the fourteen tissues the lung supplies sum to
  371.51 mL/h; the 1.49 mL/h difference is the lymph node's perfusion (1.65 mL/h in
  Table 1, within the table's rounding), which is not an antibody-transport path in
  this model. Using 373 mL/h directly opens a 0.4%
  arterial leak - roughly 1.5 mL/h - which is two orders of magnitude larger than the
  antibodies' true clearance (2.6-29 uL/h) and would dominate the terminal phase. The
  model derives `q_lu` as the sum of the non-lung arterial supplies so the arterial
  junction closes exactly.
- **Liver lymph flow.** Supplementary Methods 2 prints
  `L_LIVER = 0.002 * (PLQ_LIVER + PLQ_LIVER,UPSTREAM)`: 0.2% of the liver's total
  plasma inflow, the hepatic artery plus the portal return from spleen, pancreas and
  both intestines. The model uses this expression as printed, so it is not a
  deviation; it is listed because it differs from the rule `L_ORG = 0.002 * PLQ_ORG`
  used for every other organ. With it the liver's vascular outflow is 0.998 of its
  total inflow, as for the other organs.
- **Liver arterial supply.** Supplementary Methods 2 writes the liver's vascular
  inflow as `C_V,LIVER * (PLQ_LIVER - L_LIVER) + ...`, i.e. the liver feeding itself.
  The model uses `C_V,LUNG * PLQ_LIVER` (arterial supply from the lung) plus the four
  portal tributaries, matching the generic organ rule in the same section and
  Shah & Betts 2012 Eq 11.
- **Blood-cell sub-compartments are omitted.** Shah & Betts 2012 carries a vascular
  blood-cell space per tissue, but antibody never enters it, so those states remain
  identically zero. They do not appear in Liu 2023's Supplementary Methods 2 equations
  and are dropped here, reducing the system from 93 to 77 states with no change in
  predictions.
- **Shape of the published model curves.** The packaged model reproduces the
  clearance and exposure of the published model (see *Comparison with the published
  model curves*) but not the shape of its curves, digitized from Figures 4, 5 and 6.
  Dose divided by the 0.944 mL plasma volume is
  `r format(round(c0, -2), big.mark = ",")` ng/mL. At 2.2 h the 20 published Figure 5
  curves are still at `r round(band_pct[["lower"]])`-`r round(band_pct[["upper"]])`%
  of that, whereas the simulated curves are
  already at `r round(sim_2h_pct[1])`-`r round(sim_2h_pct[2])`%: within the first
  hour the simulated antibody occupies
  `r sprintf("%.2f", min(v_1h_mL))`-`r sprintf("%.2f", max(v_1h_mL))` mL, the plasma
  together with the organ vascular spaces of Shah & Betts 2012 Table 1, which fill at
  blood-flow rates. Later the published curves fall faster. Between 300 and 698 h the
  simulated terminal half-life is
  `r sprintf("%.2f", min(term$thalf_ratio))`-`r sprintf("%.2f", max(term$thalf_ratio))`
  times the published one across the 16 Figure 5 curves readable at both times
  (`r round(term$sim_thalf[term$k == 0])` h against
  `r round(term$pub_thalf[term$k == 0])` h at `F1` = 0.4), and the `F1` = 4 curve
  reaches 10 ng/mL at `r round(cross$sim_time[cross$k == 19])` h instead of the
  published `r cross$time[cross$k == 19]` h. In the first hours every simulated
  Figure 5 curve lies below the published ones, and at the last digitized
  time every simulated curve lies above its published counterpart. The cause is not determined. What the
  checks show is limited. The clearance and exposure checks agree with the published
  model under the per-organ pinocytosis form that Supplementary Methods 2 prints and
  the model uses, `CL_UP,ORG = CL_UP * V_E,ORG` (geometric-mean ratios
  `r sprintf("%.2f", gm_cl_all)` and `r sprintf("%.2f", gm_auc_val)`), so the
  elimination side matches; those checks do not test distribution, so they do not
  locate the difference in shape. `F2`, which the paper does not state for Figure 5,
  moves the digitized Figure 5 points by at most `r round(f2_change_pct, 1)`% between
  1 and 1.45. Liu 2023 states that all other values are those of Shah & Betts 2012 and
  publishes no model code, so the model keeps the published physiology unchanged.
- **Molar mass.** The model runs in nmol and nM, which is the natural scale for the
  FcRn binding terms. Neither Liu 2023 nor Shah & Betts 2012 reports a molar mass for
  the panel, so this vignette uses 150,000 g/mol - the nominal value for an
  aglycosylated human IgG1 - purely to convert the 2 mg/kg dose into nmol and to plot
  concentrations in ng/mL. This is **not** a paper-derived value. The primary
  validation metrics (clearance, half-life, classification against the 12 mL/day/kg
  threshold) are unaffected by the choice, because both dose and AUC scale with
  1/molar mass. AUC in `ng*h/mL`, and with it the %PE column, does not depend on it
  either: the model is linear at this dose, so the nmol dose and the ng/mL conversion
  cancel (checked in *Comparison with the published model curves*).
- **Body weight.** Liu 2023 does not state a body weight. The model is built on
  Shah & Betts 2012's 28 g mouse physiology, and 28 g is also what reconciles
  Supplementary Table S1's mg/kg dose, ng*h/mL AUC and mL/h clearance columns
  (Ab1: 56 ug / 7.97e6 ng*h/mL = 0.0070 mL/h versus 0.00687 reported), so 28 g is used
  throughout.
- **Residual error.** Liu 2023 states only that a proportional error variance model
  was assumed; no magnitude is reported in the paper or the supplement, so `propSd` is
  carried as `fixed(0)`. Simulations are therefore deterministic typical-value
  predictions.
- **No between-subject variability.** The published model has no random-effects layer;
  the 56 individually estimated `F1`/`F2` pairs of Supplementary Table S2 belong to the
  base model, not the final covariate model, and are used here only to reproduce
  Figure 3d and to check the model's clearance against Supplementary Table S1.
- **Ab87 classification inconsistency in the source.** Supplementary Table S3 lists
  Ab87 as observed fast-clearing, but Supplementary Table S1's clearance for Ab87
  (0.0121 mL/h) is 10.4 mL/day/kg at 28 g, below the paper's own 12 mL/day/kg
  threshold. The vignette reports both the transcribed Table S3 call and the
  recomputed one rather than choosing between them.
- **Half-life within the low-retention plateau.** Above the sigmoid's lower plateau
  every antibody with `HEPARIN_RT` below roughly 15 min receives the same `F1` and
  therefore an identical simulated profile, whereas the observed half-lives of those
  antibodies span 116-393 h. Liu 2023 makes the same observation ("a single F1 value
  of about 0.68 can describe PK profiles of mAbs reasonably well when Heparin_RT
  values are smaller than 16.5, despite nontrivial variability in the individually
  estimated F1"). AUC and clearance are nevertheless well reproduced (median
  predicted/observed clearance ratio `r sprintf("%.2f", training_fold$median_fold)` in
  the training panel, `r round(training_fold$within_2fold_pct)`% within 2-fold). The
  simulated half-lives are longer than the published ones partly because the model's
  terminal phase is longer than that of the published model curves (*Shape of the
  published model curves* above), and partly because they are estimated from smooth
  noise-free profiles over a 672 h window, whereas the published values come from
  sparse composite mean profiles with three animals per time point.
- **Observed concentration-time data.** The observed points overlaid in Liu 2023's
  Figures 4 and 6 are not published in machine-readable form. The figure replications
  above therefore compare model curves only, the packaged model against the published
  model curves digitized from those figures; the quantitative observed-versus-predicted
  comparison uses the NCA summaries of Supplementary Tables S1 and S3.
- **Upstream platform parameters.** `FcRn`, `Kdeg`, `C_LNLF`, `Kon`, `Koff`, `FR`,
  `sigma_IS`, the per-tissue `sigma_V` values and the entire mouse physiology are
  inherited from Shah & Betts 2012, which Liu 2023 cites as reference 36 and adopts
  unchanged apart from `CLup`. That paper was available when this model was built;
  no value was taken from any other source.
- **Parameter names describe the mechanism, not the paper's symbol.** The registry
  names each inter-antibody variability coefficient for the quantity it scales:
  `clup_scale` for the paper's `F1` (which multiplies the pinocytotic uptake `CLup`)
  and `lymph_scale` for the paper's `F2` (which multiplies organ lymphatic flow), with
  the sigmoid's shape parameters suffixed to that root (`clup_scale_min`,
  `clup_scale_max`, `rt50_clup_scale`, `hill_clup_scale`). A bare `f1` would name the
  source's notation rather than the quantity, so a consumer searching the library for
  what scales `CLup` could not find it. The paper's symbols are retained throughout
  this vignette's narrative and in each parameter's `label()` so the mapping back to
  Table 2 stays explicit.
- **`HEPARIN_RT` is a molecule-level covariate.** Every other covariate in the
  register is a property of the subject; this one is a property of the administered
  antibody, which is what makes an inter-antibody-variability analysis possible at
  all. Operationally it still behaves like an ordinary covariate column - each animal's
  records carry the retention time of the antibody it received, constant within
  subject - so it is registered under the existing "Formulation / assay / study"
  section rather than founding a separate molecule-attribute family. The remaining
  nine developability readouts measured in this paper (FcRn chromatography retention
  time, AC-SINS, HIC, BVP, membrane-prep ELISA, poly-D-lysine, PEI, calculated pI,
  thermolysin stability) are deliberately **not** registered, because no extracted
  model uses them.
